s1.syndrome_frame: Acute loss of consciousness with trauma and near-syncope episodes in an elderly patient with a history of hypertension
salient_findings: Episode of syncope with head and left shoulder pain
Near-fainting spells in the week prior to the index event
Mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with preserved left ventricular systolic function
key_facts: Patient is in their 80s
History of hypertension controlled with Dyazide
Presented with 1 episode of syncope
Felt hot and light-headed before the syncopal event
Had a few near-fainting spells in the week prior to the index event
Vital signs were stable without considerable orthostatic changes
Serum electrolyte levels and cardiac enzymes were normal
Cranial CT showed no acute pathologic changes
Echocardiogram showed mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with preserved left ventricular systolic function
ECG showed sinus rhythm with right bundle-branch block and fascicular block

shortlist.label: Vasovagal syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced syncope with preceding hot and light-headed feelings, consistent with vasovagal syncope

shortlist.label: Orthostatic hypotension
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had near-fainting spells and syncope, although orthostatic changes were not significant, it remains a possibility

shortlist.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of hypertension and presented with syncope, with ECG showing sinus rhythm and fascicular block, which could be related to cardiac sarcoidosis

shortlist.label: Aortic stenosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of hypertension and presented with syncope, with echocardiogram showing mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, which could be related to aortic stenosis

shortlist.label: Carotid sinus syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced syncope with trauma, and carotid sinus syncope is a possible cause of syncope in elderly patients with a history of hypertension

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of feeling hot and light-headed before the syncopal event, along with a few near-fainting spells prior, are consistent with vasovagal syncope. The stable vital signs without orthostatic changes and normal laboratory tests also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Orthostatic hypotension
rejected.why: Vital signs were stable without considerable orthostatic changes in blood pressure and heart rate

rejected.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Echocardiogram showed mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with preserved left ventricular systolic function, but no evidence of cardiac sarcoidosis

rejected.label: Aortic stenosis
rejected.why: Echocardiogram did not indicate aortic stenosis

rejected.label: Carotid sinus syncope
rejected.why: No specific evidence of carotid sinus hypersensitivity was mentioned
